"Midtjylland Region i alt" serves as the aggregate statistical entity for the Central Denmark Region (Region Midtjylland) within the national Akut Kirurgi Databasen (AKDB). It encompasses all hospitals in the region and provides crucial data for national quality development and benchmarking in acute surgery. As a primary subregion of [[danmark|Danmark]], it is systematically evaluated alongside national and hospital-level data to assess clinical outcomes and patient demographics [^src3].

The entity's data is central to evaluating postoperative outcomes, particularly concerning comorbidities such as cancer. In the 2023 AKDB report, "Midtjylland Region i alt" contributed to supplementary analyses on the distribution of cancer diseases among operated patients, which helps in risk-adjusting quality indicators [^src1]. It also provided aggregate demographic and procedural statistics, such as a recorded total of 801 cases in specific age and gender distributions [^src2].

In the 2024 AKDB report, the region's performance was closely monitored through supplementary quality indicators measuring 30-day mortality after acute surgery. For the period spanning September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024, the region recorded 40 deaths within 30 days among 152 included patients with a Charlson Comorbidity Index score of 1 or 2, a metric tracked under [[indikator-9b|Indikator 9b]] [^src4]. Furthermore, for patients with severe comorbidities (Charlson Score ≥ 3), the region similarly recorded 40 deaths within 30 days out of 152 included patients, which is evaluated under [[indikator-9c|Indikator 9c]] [^src4]. Additional aggregate data from the 2024 report notes a total of 807 cases in regional demographic breakdowns [^src5]. Through these metrics, "Midtjylland Region i alt" plays a vital role in identifying development potential and guiding clinical improvement initiatives in Danish acute care.
